issues.description: _BufferingHandler.buffer is unbounded and can OOM the worker on long pre-connect hangs
issues.detail: The buffer is a plain list with no size cap. A job that hangs before init_recording while emitting frequent logs (retry loops, DEBUG noise) can grow it without bound. Use a bounded deque (maxlen) or byte cap with a drop-oldest policy and dropped-records counter.

issues.description: _shutdown_telemetry removes ALL LoggingHandlers from root, including user-installed ones
issues.detail: The loop iterates root handlers and detaches every opentelemetry LoggingHandler instance, not just the one this module installed. Users with their own OTLP LoggingHandler on a separate provider will see it silently removed. Track the specific handler created by _setup_cloud_tracer and remove only that reference.

issues.description: _flush_early_log_buffer targets the first matching LoggingHandler, which may be the wrong one
issues.detail: Replay scans root.handlers and emits to the first opentelemetry LoggingHandler found. With multiple handlers (user-attached plus the one just installed), buffered crash logs may route to the wrong provider or silently no-op. Capture the specific handler in _setup_cloud_tracer and pass it through directly.

issues.description: _on_cleanup crash path forces logs=True regardless of user/server RecordingOptions
issues.detail: When _recording_initialized is False, _on_cleanup calls init_recording(RecordingOptions(logs=True, ...)) unconditionally. The PR claims to honor user-specified record settings, but server/job settings disabling log recording are silently overridden. Gate on a flag from JobInfo/JobAcceptArguments indicating logs were requested.

issues.description: init_recording invoked from _on_cleanup runs heavy cloud tracer setup on the crash/teardown path
issues.detail: _on_cleanup synchronously triggers _setup_cloud_tracer during shutdown, adding network/SDK setup that can itself hang or raise. The bare except logs but may drop buffered crash logs on partial failure, and force_flush may race a closing event loop. Verify safety at cleanup and ensure crash logs are not lost on init failure.

issues.description: Makefile drops `-n auto` parallelism and silently removes test_plugin_google_stt.py from CI
issues.detail: The unit-tests target no longer runs in parallel via pytest-xdist and excludes the Google STT plugin test file. Neither change is mentioned in the PR description. This materially slows CI and drops coverage; if intentional, document the rationale and track flakiness, otherwise revert as likely accidental local debug leakage.

synthesis.summary: The PR's core mechanism — buffer early logs and replay them through OTLP when a session crashes before init_recording — is sound, but multiple sharp edges need work. Consensus concerns: the buffer is unbounded (OOM risk), _shutdown_telemetry detaches all LoggingHandlers globally rather than just the one it installed, replay matches the first handler instead of a tracked reference, and the cleanup-time init_recording both ignores user RecordingOptions and runs heavy setup on the teardown path. Unrelated makefile changes (disabling pytest-xdist, removing the google STT test) should be justified or reverted before merge.
